instruction: Mute the audio in VLC media player.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires muting audio in VLC. Agent can use keyboard shortcut 'M' or Audio > Mute menu. Custom getter checks volume level from VLC HTTP status.xml (volume=0 indicates muted), metric compares boolean result.
metadata.verification: VLC mute: When muted, volume is set to 0. Getter checks <volume> element from status.xml, returns true if volume=0.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter conflates 'volume=0' with 'muted state', which are distinct concepts in VLC media player
VLC has a separate mute toggle independent of volume level - a user can have volume=50 and still be muted, or volume=0 without being in mute state
This could lead to false positives (volume=0 but not actually muted) or false negatives (volume>0 but muted via mute button)
The verification logic checks the wrong state indicator and won't correctly capture whether the mute button/command was activated
VLC is launched with '--no-audio' flag which may affect how mute state is represented in status.xml
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Investigate VLC's status.xml structure to identify the actual mute state element (likely a boolean field or flag separate from the volume element)
Update the getter to check the correct mute state indicator instead of assuming volume==0 means muted
Test the actual VLC status.xml response when mute button is pressed vs when volume is set to 0 to understand the difference
Consider checking both volume level AND a dedicated mute flag if VLC maintains both states independently
